paper_title: Unsupervised Process Reward Models — Eq. 6 LLM-as-a-Judge control
prompt_text: You will be shown a math problem and a proposed step-by-step solution. After each step, a marker has been inserted: "+" means the step is correct, "-" means the step is incorrect. Assess each step in order and predict the marker that belongs there.

signal_definitions.marker_logprobs: next-token log-probabilities of the '+'/'-' marker tokens at each step boundary, renormalised over {+,-}
signal_definitions.S_j: Eq. 6 cumulative score for candidate first-error step j

declared_deviations.we_do: literal ' +' / ' -' with a convention-explaining system message, marker token ids derived per following-context
declared_deviations.why: no released prompt; a raw solution gives the model no reason to read those characters as evaluative

declared_deviations.paper_says: one marked sequence per candidate j
declared_deviations.we_do: one all-'+' pass, S(j) as a cumulative sum
declared_deviations.why: steps before j are '+' for every j, so the boundary distributions are identical across candidates — algebraically equivalent, T-times cheaper

extra.not_uprm: this is the paper's own Eq. 6 control, not the trained uPRM
